beats.text: We long for the world to make sense. The world answers with silence.
Camus called that collision the absurd — a mind demanding meaning from a universe that offers none.
He said it forces one real question: if life has no given meaning, why go on living at all?
His answer was defiance. Don't lie about the silence. Don't leap to false comfort. And don't quit.
Live anyway — fully, lucidly, in revolt against the meaninglessness, without pretending it isn't there.
The absurd hero doesn't win. He simply refuses to look away, and lives harder because of it.
The point is not to resolve the silence. It is to stay — awake, and alive, inside it.

attribution: Albert Camus · The Myth of Sisyphus
